pairs.subject: authorization
pairs.evidence: app/api/workspaces/[id]/members/[userId]/route.ts:58 A privilege-escalation attempt (granting a role above the caller's ceiling) is refused with a bare 403 and nothing records it. Across this context the capability, membership and credential denials are all answered without a trail line or a denial counter, so a probe and a misconfiguration cannot be told apart.

techniques.evidence: app/api/workspaces/[id]/members/[userId]/route.ts:58 Silent gate: grep over app/api/auth, workspaces, workspace, ops and health finds no audit or denial logging. The only console.error is logout's revocation-write failure. /api/ops shows rate-limit refusal counts but no authorization-denial rate.

app/api/route-capability-coverage.test.ts:85 Requirements are imperative in-handler calls (`const denied = await requireX(...)`), detected by a regex over the source. The ratchet's own allowlist admits dozens of mutating doors marked 'not yet judged', so a working operation can still exist without a declared requirement. Totality does not hold.

app/api/workspaces/route.ts:65 Non-public handlers are reached through the session entry (withSession/withWorkspace), which re-asserts the proxy's 401 as a handler-side tripwire. The capability half of the decision is not at the chokepoint; that gap is recorded under declarative-requirements, not counted twice.

app/api/auth/switch-workspace/route.ts:63 A demo session fails closed on its origin workspace. A revoked cookie gets the absent-cookie 401. An issuer refusal clears the cookie and answers 401 (error voids the result), and a thrown error goes to the 500 catch, never to a mint.

app/api/health/route.ts:70 The health probe splits its payload by tier: public verdict / trusted engines / home-org host detail. Its detail inherits the tier of the resource it exposes. The import dry-run plan is also gated identically to apply (requireOperator + org:manage before planOrgRestore), so the preview inherits the tier of its action.

app/api/auth/switch-workspace/route.ts:100 For a non-admin, GET /api/workspaces lists only teams they belong to (route.ts:36). But switch-workspace answers 403 for a same-org team they cannot see and 404 for an unknown id, and PATCH /api/workspaces/[id] behaves the same way through requireWorkspaceCapability. So the write refusal confirms existence the read hides. The cross-org boundary does borrow the read's 404 correctly. Low severity: ids are random ws_ ids.

app/api/workspaces/[id]/members/[userId]/route.ts:49 An unrecognized role is refused against the closed role vocabulary. The next line intersects the requested role with callerDelegationCeiling() and refuses rather than clamps, so nobody can grant above what they hold.

app/api/workspaces/route.ts:73 KP_MULTI_WORKSPACE is fixed for the process, yet it runs as a request-time 403 inside the handler, after the capability check. KP_SIGNUP_ENABLED is the same: register hand-mimics a 404 inside the handler. Elsewhere the proxy already removes a surface by rewrite (KP_JOBSEEKER). The GET does expose `multiWorkspace` as a queryable mode, which partly meets the 'state the mode' rule.

app/api/workspaces/route.ts:36 Tenancy is an SQL predicate over shared better-sqlite3 tables, not an owner-composed storage address. Legitimate org-admin reads span teams, which is the case the technique says it does not fit.
